notes.meaning: God spoke to the prophet Ezekiel and gave him a new message. This prophecy announced God's coming judgment against an ancient enemy of His people.

God commands Ezekiel to turn his face toward Mount Seir and speak against it. Mount Seir was the mountainous home of Edom, the descendants of Jacob's brother Esau. In Scripture, Edom stands as a symbol of all nations that hate God's people.
The Lord God announces that He is actively opposing Mount Seir. He will raise His powerful hand against the nation to turn its land into a barren wasteland.
The cities of Edom will be completely broken down and turned into empty ruins. When their destruction is complete, the people will recognize that the Lord is God.

The Edomites held a bitter, long-standing hatred toward Israel that stretched back to their early ancestors. When Jerusalem fell and the Israelites suffered their worst crisis, Edom took advantage of their weakness and helped slaughter them.
The Lord makes a solemn promise that Edom will now face the very bloodshed it loved to cause. Because they took pleasure in cruelty and murder, violent destruction will hunt them down.
God declares that Mount Seir will become a totally abandoned waste. The busy trade roads that once made the nation rich will be emptied, and regular travelers will disappear.
The mountains, valleys, and dry riverbeds of Edom will be covered with fallen soldiers. Invading armies will cut them down wherever they try to hide.
Edom will be left in permanent ruins, and its towns will never be restored or lived in again. This permanent downfall will prove to everyone that the Lord is God.
Edom boldly claimed that it would take over the lands of both Israel and Judah after their defeat. They failed to realize that the Lord still claimed that land as His own and was still present there.
God promises to punish Edom with the exact same anger, jealousy, and cruelty that Edom showed to His people. When the Lord brings this judgment, He will reveal His protecting care to Israel.
The Edomites assumed the mountains of Israel were completely abandoned and ready to be devoured. God wants them to know that He personally heard every mocking and insulting word they spoke.
When the Edomites spoke arrogantly against Israel, they were really bragging against God Himself. The Lord warns that not one of their proud, boastful words escaped His notice.
When the rest of the surrounding world is blessed with peace and joy, Edom will remain completely desolate. Those who celebrate the troubles of others will be left to mourn alone.

Edom cheered when Israel lost its land, so the Lord will give Edom the exact same fate. All of Mount Seir and the entire region of Edom will become desolate, proving to the nations that the Lord is God.
